findings.summary: Aryam Investment 1 secured two of five board seats at World Liberty Financial. The two Aryam-appointed directors are Martin Edelman (G42 general counsel, Paul Hastings senior counsel, adviser to Royal Group and Mubadala) and Peng Xiao (G42 CEO). Both also serve as directors of MGX. Other WLFI board members include Eric Trump and Zach Witkoff. WLFI website does not list Edelman or Xiao on its team page.

Quid pro quo timeline: Jan 16 2025 - Aryam deal signed (500M for 49% WLFI). Jan 20 2025 - Trump inaugurated. Mar 2025 - Sheikh Tahnoon visits White House, meets Trump and Witkoff. May 2025 - Trump admin announces UAE gets access to 500K advanced AI chips annually. Biden had blocked this over fears technology would reach China through G42 (which had close Huawei ties). Apr 2024 - G42 had divested from China as condition of Microsoft 1.5B investment, but divested entities went to another Tahnoon fund.

MGX (another Tahnoon-led entity, co-founded by G42 and Mubadala) used WLFI USD1 stablecoin to settle a 2B investment in Binance - the largest single crypto investment ever paid in stablecoin. MGX and WLFI share management/board members (G42 executives). This creates a circular financial ecosystem: Tahnoon entity buys into WLFI, another Tahnoon entity uses WLFI product for a massive transaction. Congress investigating whether USD1 usage in Binance deal influenced Trump pardon of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (pardoned Oct 21 2025).

Multiple Congressional investigations launched: (1) Rep Ro Khanna (D-CA), ranking member House Select Committee on CCP, sent formal letter Feb 4 2026 to WLFI demanding ownership records, payment details, cap tables, profit distributions, board appointment records, due diligence materials by Mar 1 2026. (2) Sens Warren and Kim demanded CFIUS review by Treasury Sec Bessent with Mar 5 2026 deadline. (3) Rep Kamlager-Dove pursuing investigation into corrupt Trump-UAE AI chip deal. WLFI denies wrongdoing, calls probe politically motivated.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: Aryam Investment 1 not found in: SEC EDGAR (0 hits), GLEIF (4 results all unrelated Indian entities), OCCRP Aleph (0 hits), ICIJ offshore leaks (0 hits), UK Companies House (API error but unlikely presence), US corporate registries (only unrelated FL entities), FARA (0 hits for Aryam, no UAE registration found). No LEI registered for Aryam Investment 1. Not registered as a foreign agent. No SEC filings. Entity is opaque by design - incorporated in jurisdictions (Delaware and Abu Dhabi) with minimal disclosure requirements.

Aryam Investment 1 is a purpose-built SPV backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan that acquired 49% of World Liberty Financial for $500M. Two identically named entities were separately incorporated in Delaware and Abu Dhabi on consecutive days in Dec 2024, ~1 week after Steve Witkoff's UAE trip. The Abu Dhabi entity shares an office address with other Tahnoon companies. No ownership information disclosed in either jurisdiction.

Aryam Investment 1 signed agreement Jan 16 2025 for 49% stake in WLFI for $500M. Payment in two tranches: $250M upfront (Jan 2025) and $250M due by July 15 2025. Of initial $250M: $187M to Trump family entities DT Marks DEFI LLC and DT Marks SC LLC, $31M to Witkoff-affiliated entities, remaining to Folkman/Herro entities. Distribution of second tranche undetermined by WSJ.

Aryam WLFI deal timeline suggests quid pro quo with US AI chip exports. Jan 16 2025: Aryam signs $500M deal. Jan 20: Trump inaugurated. May 2025: US agrees to allow UAE to purchase 500K+ advanced Nvidia AI chips annually, with ~1/5 allocated to Tahnoon's G42. Person close to Tahnoon said deal funded by sheikh and co-investors, not G42 funds. Congress (Ro Khanna, Warren, Kim) launched probes. Warren/Kim demanded CFIUS review with Mar 5 2026 deadline.

MGX (another Tahnoon investment vehicle) invested $2B in Binance in May 2025, using World Liberty Financial's USD1 stablecoin for settlement. This created a revenue stream for WLFI (in which Aryam/Tahnoon held 49%) and boosted USD1's profile. Zach Witkoff announced USD1 as official settlement stablecoin. This circular structure means Tahnoon entities are both WLFI's largest shareholder AND its largest stablecoin customer.

The name Aryam is Arabic, meaning white deer or gazelle. No evidence found of other numbered Aryam Investment entities (2, 3, etc). The numbering suggests a series structure was planned but only one entity appears publicly. No LEI record exists for Aryam Investment 1 in GLEIF. No SEC EDGAR filings. No OpenSanctions or OCCRP Aleph records. No SSL certificates or web presence. No UK Companies House registration. Entity appears to be a clean SPV with no digital footprint.

curation.lead:
Aryam Investment 1 is a special purpose vehicle controlled by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE national security adviser and brother of the UAE president. Incorporated simultaneously in Delaware and Abu Dhabi in December 2024, the entity was created for a single transaction: the acquisition of a 49% stake in World Liberty Financial for $500 million [Finding #3980]. The agreement was signed on January 16, 2025 — four days before the presidential inauguration — by Eric Trump on behalf of WLFI and by Martin Edelman and Peng Xiao, both senior executives at Tahnoon’s artificial intelligence firm G42, on behalf of Aryam [Finding #4265]. The deal was never publicly disclosed; it came to light only through a Wall Street Journal investigation in February 2026 [Finding #4168].

Of the first $250 million tranche paid at signing, $187 million flowed to Trump family entities DT Marks DEFI LLC and DT Marks SC LLC, approximately $31 million went to entities affiliated with Steve Witkoff — then serving as Trump’s special envoy to the Middle East — and further sums reached co-founders Zach Folkman and Chase Herro [Finding #4123]. Aryam secured two of five WLFI board seats for Edelman and Peng Xiao, though neither appeared on WLFI’s public team page [Finding #3981]. Extensive searches of SEC EDGAR, GLEIF, OCCRP Aleph, ICIJ offshore leaks, FARA, and multiple corporate registries returned no records for the entity, indicating it was designed for minimal public footprint [Finding #3992].

The transaction sits at the center of multiple congressional investigations and a broader pattern connecting sovereign Gulf capital to Trump family financial interests. Months after the deal closed, another Tahnoon vehicle, MGX, used WLFI’s USD1 stablecoin to settle a $2 billion investment in Binance — creating a circular financial ecosystem in which Tahnoon entities functioned as both WLFI’s largest shareholder and its largest stablecoin customer [Finding #4132]. Senators Warren and Kim demanded a CFIUS review of the Aryam deal, while the House Select Committee on the CCP issued a 16-question demand letter to WLFI with a March 1, 2026 deadline [Finding #3988].
curation.system_role: Aryam Investment 1 is the financial instrument through which Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth, channeled via Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan's G42 executives, acquired a controlling minority stake in the Trump family's cryptocurrency venture days before the inauguration. Its structural significance lies in three dimensions: first, as the vehicle for the largest known single payment from a foreign sovereign-linked entity to Trump family interests ($187M in the first tranche alone); second, as the node connecting UAE AI and defense technology ambitions to US policy reversals on chip exports; and third, as a case study in opacity — a dual-jurisdiction SPV with no regulatory filings, no web presence, and no public disclosure, revealed only through investigative journalism thirteen months after execution.

sections.title: Corporate Structure and Beneficial Ownership
sections.content:
Aryam Investment 1 exists as a dual-entity structure: two identically named companies incorporated separately in Delaware and Abu Dhabi on consecutive days in December 2024, approximately one week after Steve Witkoff’s trip to the UAE [Finding #4121]. The Delaware entity is managed by Martin Edelman, G42’s general counsel and senior counsel at Paul Hastings, and by Peng Xiao, G42’s chief executive officer [Finding #3979]. The Abu Dhabi entity shares office space in the Abu Dhabi Global Market area with other companies in Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan’s business empire. A person close to Tahnoon told reporters the deal was funded by the sheikh and unnamed co-investors, not by G42 corporate funds [Finding #4130].

The entity’s name, Arabic for “white gazelle,” carries the suffix “1,” suggesting a planned series of investment vehicles, though no Aryam Investment 2 or subsequent entities have surfaced [Finding #4138]. Searches across SEC EDGAR, GLEIF, OCCRP Aleph, ICIJ offshore leaks, FARA, OpenSanctions, UK Companies House, and US state corporate registries returned zero results, confirming the entity has no regulatory filings, no Legal Entity Identifier, no foreign agent registration, and no web presence [Finding #3992]. The choice of Delaware and Abu Dhabi — both jurisdictions with minimal beneficial ownership disclosure requirements — appears deliberate. Aryam functions as a clean special purpose vehicle designed to insulate the ultimate beneficial owners from public scrutiny.

sections.title: The $500 Million WLFI Acquisition
sections.content:
On January 16, 2025 — four days before the presidential inauguration — Eric Trump signed an agreement on behalf of World Liberty Financial transferring a 49% stake to Aryam Investment 1 for $500 million [Finding #3980]. Martin Edelman and Peng Xiao signed for Aryam [Finding #4265]. The transaction was structured in two tranches: $250 million at signing and a second $250 million due by July 15, 2025 [Finding #4123]. Of the initial payment, $187 million flowed to Trump family entities DT Marks DEFI LLC and DT Marks SC LLC, approximately $31 million went to entities affiliated with Steve Witkoff, and further funds reached Zach Folkman and Chase Herro [Finding #4123]. The deal reduced DT Marks DeFi LLC’s equity from 60% to 40% [Finding #3835].

As part of the acquisition, Aryam secured two of five WLFI board seats for Edelman and Peng Xiao — both of whom also serve as directors of MGX, another Tahnoon investment vehicle [Finding #3981]. Critically, Aryam was not granted rights to future WLFI token sales, excluding the Tahnoon entity from what was at the time the company’s sole revenue stream [Finding #4266]. The deal was never publicly disclosed by either party. WLFI’s website did not list Edelman or Peng Xiao on its team page despite their board seats [Finding #3981]. The Wall Street Journal broke the story in February 2026, more than thirteen months after signing [Finding #4168]. As of February 2026, neither WLFI nor Aryam had confirmed whether the second $250 million tranche was paid by the July 15, 2025 deadline [Finding #4231].

sections.title: The Tahnoon Financial Ecosystem
sections.content:
Aryam Investment 1 is one node in a constellation of entities controlled by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE national security adviser whom Fortune has called the “spy sheikh” and the New York Times described as “the A.I. world’s trillion-dollar money man” [Finding #5065] [Finding #5066]. Tahnoon chairs G42, the Abu Dhabi artificial intelligence company that received a $1.5 billion investment from Microsoft in April 2024 after divesting its Chinese operations — though those divested entities were transferred to another Tahnoon-controlled fund rather than sold to unaffiliated parties [Finding #3983]. He also leads MGX, a sovereign technology investment vehicle co-founded by G42 and Mubadala, and ADQ, an Abu Dhabi developmental holding company managing over $150 billion [Finding #5066].

The interconnection between these vehicles and WLFI created a circular financial structure. In May 2025, MGX used WLFI’s USD1 stablecoin to settle a $2 billion investment in Binance — the largest single cryptocurrency investment ever paid in stablecoin [Finding #4132]. Zachary Witkoff announced USD1 as the official settlement instrument. Because Aryam held 49% of WLFI and MGX shared board members with Aryam, Tahnoon entities were simultaneously WLFI’s largest shareholder and its largest stablecoin customer [Finding #3985]. Network analysis identified the cluster of Aryam, G42, Martin Edelman, Peng Xiao, Tahnoon, and World Liberty Financial as the largest fully connected clique in the investigation graph — a parallel power center operating entirely without US government nodes [Finding #5440].

sections.title: Policy Implications and Quid Pro Quo Timeline
sections.content:
The chronology surrounding the Aryam deal traces a pattern in which sovereign Abu Dhabi capital preceded favorable US policy shifts. On January 16, 2025, Aryam signed the $500 million agreement. Four days later, Trump was inaugurated. In March 2025, Sheikh Tahnoon visited the White House and met with both Trump and Witkoff. In May 2025, the Trump administration announced that the UAE would receive access to over 500,000 advanced Nvidia AI chips annually, with approximately one-fifth allocated to G42 [Finding #3983] [Finding #4130]. The Biden administration had blocked this access over concerns that technology would reach China through G42’s extensive Huawei ties. On May 12, 2025, Trump formally rescinded Biden-era AI chip export restrictions to Gulf states [Finding #5444].

Congress investigated whether this amounted to a quid pro quo. The MGX-Binance settlement in USD1 stablecoin also raised questions about whether the use of a Trump family financial product influenced the October 21, 2025 presidential pardon of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao [Finding #3985]. The Aryam deal signed four days before inauguration formed part of a broader coordinated action window identified by temporal analysis: on inauguration week alone, the incoming administration simultaneously revoked ethics executive orders, established DOGE, placed operatives at DHS, signed five immigration executive orders, and began dismissing SEC cryptocurrency enforcement cases [Finding #5446]. The compression of these actions suggests pre-planned institutional positioning rather than improvised policy development.

sections.title: Congressional Investigations and Regulatory Status
sections.content:
The revelation of the Aryam deal triggered multiple congressional inquiries. Representative Ro Khanna, ranking member of the House Select Committee on the CCP, sent a formal letter to World Liberty Financial on February 4, 2026, demanding ownership records, payment details, capitalization tables, profit distributions, board appointment records, and all communications related to the Binance deal by March 1, 2026 [Finding #3988]. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Andy Kim demanded that Treasury Secretary Bessent initiate a CFIUS review of the Aryam acquisition by March 5, 2026, citing national security concerns over UAE access to WLFI user data. Representative Sydney Kamlager-Dove pursued a separate investigation into the connection between the investment and the AI chip export reversal [Finding #3988].

Aryam’s governance rights at WLFI remain partially opaque. The entity holds two of five board seats and a 49% equity stake, but no public disclosure has addressed whether Aryam possesses veto rights, consent rights, or other protective provisions beyond board representation [Finding #4266]. As of the March 5, 2026 deadline imposed by Warren and Kim, no formal CFIUS review had been initiated. Given that the Trump administration controls the Treasury Department — which chairs CFIUS — the likelihood of a self-initiated national security review of a transaction benefiting the president’s family was assessed as minimal [Finding #4283]. WLFI denied wrongdoing and characterized the probes as politically motivated.

open_questions: Was the second $250 million tranche paid by the July 15, 2025 deadline? Neither WLFI nor Aryam has disclosed the status of this payment, and the WSJ reported it could not determine the allocation of remaining funds. The outcome materially affects whether the Trump family entities ultimately received up to $375 million from this single transaction.

Who are the unnamed co-investors alongside Sheikh Tahnoon in the Aryam vehicle? A source close to Tahnoon stated the funds did not come from G42 corporate accounts, implying personal or sovereign wealth participation. The identities of these co-investors would reveal whether other Gulf sovereign entities or private individuals hold indirect stakes in the Trump family's cryptocurrency venture.

What protective provisions does Aryam hold beyond its two board seats? Standard minority investor protections for a 49% stake would typically include consent rights over major transactions, dilution protections, and information rights. The absence of public disclosure about these terms leaves the full extent of UAE sovereign influence over WLFI undetermined.

Did any communication occur between Aryam-affiliated individuals and US government officials regarding AI chip export policy between January and May 2025? The temporal proximity between the $500 million investment, Tahnoon's March White House visit, and the May reversal of Biden-era chip export restrictions to the UAE raises the question of whether the investment functioned as consideration for policy changes.

Does Aryam Investment 1 hold any FARA-triggering obligations? The entity is controlled by the UAE national security adviser and placed directors on the board of a company generating policy-relevant revenue for the president's family, yet no foreign agent registration has been filed.
